name: Remorse-Tidal

civilization.name: The Penitent Depths
civilization.notes: An aquatic civilization that retreated beneath the waves after a surface catastrophe they believe they caused. They practice ritual atonement and refuse all contact with off-worlders.

geological_features: Shallow continental shelves with coral-analogous reefs
Tidal flats exposed during the planet's extreme low tides
specific_features: Sunken cities visible through clear shallows, deliberately flooded by their own inhabitants
Bioluminescent warning buoys marking forbidden zones
description: Remorse-Tidal is an oceanic world of shallow, crystalline seas where sunlight penetrates to the seabed and the ruins of once-great cities lie visible beneath the gentle waves. Vast tidal flats emerge during the planet's extreme gravitational cycles, exposing coral reefs and the skeletal architecture of a drowned civilization.

The atmosphere is sweet and salt-tinged, and the quality of light through the shallow water creates an effect like stained glass stretching to the horizon. There is a beauty here inseparable from sadness, the loveliness of something irretrievably lost.

The Penitent Depths deliberately flooded their own surface cities three centuries ago following an ecological disaster they attribute to their industrial expansion. They retreated into submarine habitats and sealed their history behind ritual prohibitions, practicing a culture of perpetual atonement that has calcified into religious law.

Bioluminescent warning buoys mark the boundaries beyond which off-worlders are not welcome, and the few attempts to force contact have ended in the silent destruction of survey drones. The medicinal compounds harvested from the reefs show promise against radiation sickness, creating a moral dilemma for those who would respect the Penitent Depths' isolation.
